newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Chirac dips in poll after gains.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac dips in poll after gains.

text.p: Public support for French President Jacques Chirac has dipped after rising three months in a row, an opinion poll showed on Thursday.

The survey, by the Louis Harris Institute for Valeurs Actuelles magazine, showed that 35 percent of voters had a favourable impression of conservative Chirac's performance in April, down from 40 percent a month earlier.
The number with a poor impression climbed to 60 percent from 54.

Prime Minister Alain Juppe's rating also declined after three months of gains with just 31 percent rating his performance good against 33 percent in March. The percentage with a bad impression climbed to 65 percent from 62.
And 64 percent reckoned that the economic and social climate was worsening in France, little changed from 65 percent the month before. Unemployment is at a record 12.8 percent.

The poll also showed that 39 percent of voters would pick a candidate of the ruling centre-right if parliamentary elections were held next Sunday, against 26 percent who would choose an opposition Socialist.
The poll, of 1,002 adults questioned on April 4 and 5, also indicated that 15 percent would choose a far-right National Front candidate, 10 percent a Communist and eight percent an ecologist.
Elections to the National Assembly are due in March 1998, but Chirac has the power to call them earlier.
